english: Let $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a differentiable function with $f(1)=1$. For every $x>0$, the tangent to the curve $y=f(x)$ at the point $P(x,f(x))$ meets the $y$-axis at a point whose ordinate is $f(x)\left(1-x^{2}\log_{e}x\right)$. Then $f\left(\sqrt{e}\right)$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए $f(1)=1$ है। प्रत्येक $x>0$ के लिए, वक्र $y=f(x)$ के बिन्दु $P(x,f(x))$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखा $y$-अक्ष को ऐसे बिन्दु पर मिलती है जिसकी कोटि $f(x)\left(1-x^{2}\log_{e}x\right)$ है। तब $f\left(\sqrt{e}\right)$ बराबर है
solution: Tangent at $P$: $Y-y=y'(X-x)$; at $X=0$ the ordinate is $y-xy'$
solution_full: Write $y=f(x)$. The tangent at $P(x,y)$ is $Y-y=y'(X-x)$. Putting $X=0$ gives the ordinate of its point on the $y$-axis: $Y=y-xy'$.
The given condition is $y-xy'=y\left(1-x^{2}\log_{e}x\right)=y-x^{2}y\log_{e}x$. Cancelling $y$ and dividing by $x>0$ gives $y'=xy\log_{e}x$.

Integrate the right side by parts with $u=\log_{e}x$, $dv=x\,dx$: $\displaystyle\int x\log_{e}x\,dx=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\log_{e}x-\int\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\log_{e}x-\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}$.
Therefore $f(\sqrt{e})=e^{1/4}$. Dropping the $-\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}$ term gives (A); a sign slip in the by-parts step gives (B).
originality_note: New: the curve is defined by where its tangent meets the y-axis, the intercept condition y - xy' = y(1 - x^2 ln x) turns into the separable equation y'/y = x ln x, and the evaluation point sqrt(e) makes the two by-parts terms cancel (way 5). Closest known: curves defined by a y-intercept of the tangent (usually giving linear equations); integral of x ln x. Different because: the intercept is proportional to y, so the equation is separable, and the answer depends on handling both by-parts terms correctly.
key_step: Translating the tangent's y-intercept into y'/y = x ln x, then integrating x ln x by parts and fixing the constant.
justification: Three linked stages (tangent intercept, separation, by parts) with a by-parts sign trap the options exploit. Above the plain separable DE 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) because the equation must first be extracted from a geometric condition; comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2) plus one stage.

concept_use.Integration by parts: The integral of x ln x needed after separating variables is found by parts: (x^2/2) ln x - x^2/4.
concept_use.Variable separable equations: The tangent condition gives y'/y = x ln x, a variables separable equation solved with f(1) = 1 fixing the constant.
